citation: Ma R, Yin Y, Zhang J-P, Zhang M-X, Zhou J-R, He Y, Gai W, Zhang X-H, Wang Y, Xu L-P, Liu K-Y, Huang X-J, Sun Y-Q. Metagenomic Next-generation Sequencing Compared With Blood Culture as First-line Diagnostic Method for Bloodstream Infection in Hematologic Patients With Febrile Neutropenia: A Multicenter, Prospective Study. Open Forum Infectious Diseases. 2025;12:ofaf288.
study_design: Multicenter, prospective diagnostic accuracy study (4 Chinese hematologic centers; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05149547); double-blinded with independent 4-specialist adjudication panel

population.population_description: Hematologic patients >=15 y with neutropenia (ANC <0.5x10^9/L) and fever at FN onset; chemotherapy 192 (64%), auto-HSCT 23 (8%), allo-HSCT 85 (28%); classified as definite BSI 62, probable BSI 61, other infectious FN 116, noninfectious FN 55, indeterminate 6
population.haemato_subtypes: AML 167 (56%), ALL 56 (19%), MDS 15 (5%), aplastic anemia 6 (2%), lymphoma 6 (4%), multiple myeloma 13 (4%), other 37 (12%)

neutropenic_status: Neutropenia defined as ANC <0.5 x 10^9/L; peripheral blood collected at FN onset

specimens.type: peripheral blood (whole blood: plasma + blood cell layer mNGS)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS of whole blood (plasma cfDNA + blood cell layer) (Supplementary methods; details in supplement)
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA (viruses excepted from positivity count; bacterial/fungal DNA)

reference_standard: Independent expert panel (4 hematology specialists) adjudication into definite/probable BSI, other infectious FN, noninfectious FN, indeterminate; double-blinding of clinicians and mNGS analysis team

comparator_2x2.against: final adjudicated diagnosis (definite BSI, n=62 vs noninfectious FN, n=55); Table 3, whole blood mNGS
comparator_2x2.note: Also reported: blood cell layer alone TP 24/FN 38/FP 0/TN 55 (sens 38.7%, spec 100%); plasma alone TP 56/FN 6/FP 3/TN 52 (sens 90.3%, spec 94.6%). Probable BSI (n=61) excluded from 2x2.

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: mNGS positive in 204/300 (68.0%, excluding viruses); 80/204 (39.2%) polymicrobial; BC positive 62/300 (20.7%); mNGS-BC positive agreement 79.0% (49/62), negative agreement 34.9% (83/238)

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Most Gram-positive bacteria and fungi detected exclusively by mNGS; of 62 definite BSI, mNGS positive in 60 vs BC 62 positive overall; 3 BC-positive/mNGS-negative definite BSI (contaminant-likely pathogens S. gordonii, P. mirabilis, P. humerusii); 3 mNGS-positive/noninfectious FN false positives.
turnaround_time: mNGS 39.7 +/- 15.0 hours vs BC 119.8 +/- 31.9 hours (P significant)
therapy_change: Secondary endpoint (antimicrobial management significance) - detailed counts in Supplementary Table 5, not in main text

quality_flags.blinding_of_index_result: yes (clinical physician and mNGS analysis team double-blinded; adjudication by independent expert panel)
quality_flags.overlap_risk: 35 patients contributed 2 FN events (event-level analysis); adjudication categories defined partly relative to mNGS/BC concordance

quadas2_notes: Strongest study of the set: prospective, multicenter, consecutive, double-blinded, pre-registered. Caution: 'definite BSI' definition incorporates BC/mNGS concordance (mNGS concordant with BC = definite causative pathogen), creating partial incorporation for concordant cases; discordant cases adjudicated clinically. Probable BSI (n=61) excluded from 2x2.

evidence_quotes.quote: This study was prospectively performed in 4 Chinese hematologic centers. ... The clinical physician and mNGS analysis team were double-blinded, and the adjudication of the clinical diagnosis was evaluated by another expert panel of 4 specialists.
demonstrating high sensitivity (95.2%), specificity (94.6%), and significantly shorter turnaround time (39.7 vs 119.8 hours).
This multicenter prospective study was performed in 4 Chinese hematologic centers from October 2021 to August 2022.
The diagnosis includes 62 definite BSI, 61 probable BSI, 116 infectious FN other than BSI, 55 non-infectious FN events, and 6 FN of indeterminate cause.
Among the 300 FN events, mNGS was positive in 204 (68.0%) cases (except viruses), and 80 of the 204 (39.2%) mNGS results were polymicrobial.
Among the 300 FN events, BC was positive in 62 (20.7%) cases.
The positive and negative percentage agreements of mNGS with BC were 79.0% (49/62) and 34.9% (83/238), respectively.
Compared with BC, the diagnostic time of mNGS was significantly shorter (39.7 ± 15.0 vs 119.8 ± 31.9 hours

Among the 62 definite BSI cases, mNGS was positive in 60. Among these 60 positive detections, mNGS results were adjudged as true positives in 59 cases (definite causative pathogen in 49 cases, probable causative pathogen in 7 cases, and possible causative pathogen in 3 cases).
